supplementsApproval.effect: Additive. The approval, its pinned helpers and every existing campaign receipt remain exactly as recorded.

defect.cause: controlView() keeps the Cloud Run service buildConfig, whose build name, source archive and shared image tag change on every legitimate deployment, and it has no allowance for the Google-managed framework fields a redeploy adds or drops. The sealed tests use synthetic Cloud Run services without a buildConfig, so the defect was not exercised before production.
defect.consequence: The sealed proof cannot pass for any real redeploy. Readback admission, private custody, the public projection and closure assembly all depend on it.

disclosures.topic: FUNCTION_SIGNATURE_TYPE removal departs from the Build 28 rule
disclosures.detail: The committed Build 28 comparator (tools/release/reviewedBackendControls.js at d513843e) admitted only the platform addition of FUNCTION_SIGNATURE_TYPE=http on HTTP callables and refused removal ('Existing HTTP signature cannot be replaced or removed'). This adjudication also admits the two observed removals, on beginGlobalPullRun and completePlannedJobExecution, value http, on HTTP callables only. http is the Functions Framework default for an HTTP target, so invocation is unchanged, but this is a departure from an earlier reviewed rule and needs the owner's explicit acceptance.

disclosures.topic: Why the sealed helper failed where Build 28 did not
disclosures.detail: The Build 28 comparator is written for 15 existing plus 4 new functions and refuses the Build 29 fleet, so a new helper was written for Build 29. That helper kept the Cloud Run buildConfig in its control view and did not carry over the Build 28 handling of the signature variable. Its tests use synthetic Cloud Run services without a buildConfig.

committedGateImpact: None. The committed release gate reads the closure's decision, deployment and controlBoundary fields and the final readbacks, not the control-comparison decision. The committed validateDeploymentIamBoundary requires only controlBoundary.iamMutated === false for this campaign, and validateRulesDeploymentBoundary does not read the control comparison. No change on main is needed, so the approval's stop-if-main-moves condition is unaffected.
executionNotes: The Rules phase does not consume the preservation proof. It can run through the sealed Invoke-ReviewedBackendCohort.ps1 unchanged, validation first and then -Execute, once the owner lifts the hold.
